newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel orders additional security boost.
newsitem.headline: Israel orders additional security boost.

text.p: Israel said on Saturday it was further increasing security in its towns and cities and along lines bordering the West Bank and Gaza Strip after Wednesday's twin suicide bombing in Jerusalem.

Police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin said the decision to step up security, already boosted following the fatal bombings, had been taken by Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani and police chief Assaf Hefetz.
The Islamic militant bombers killed 13 other people when they blew themselves up in Jerusalem's main Jewish market on Wednesday in the worst attack in Israel for more than a year.
"After consultation, Mr Kahalani and the police commissioner decided to reinforce police forces in crowded areas all over the country," Menuhin said.
More checkpoints would be set up and activities by Israeli civil guards boosted "in order to foster security".
Kahalani and Hefetz had also ordered more forces to lines along the West Bank and Gaza Strip, which Israel closed off on Wednesday when it barred Palestinians from entering its territory.
They had also urged Israelis to be more alert to potential threats, Menuhin said.
It was not immediately clear whether the step was taken in response to a demand for the release of all Palestinian prisoners by Sunday night made in a leaflet that claimed the attack on Wednesday.

The leaflet was issued in the name of the militant Islamic movement Hamas and set a nine p.m. (1800 GMT) deadline on Sunday for the demand to be met without saying what would happen if Israel failed to act.
Israeli officials say they are not certain it is authentic. A second Hamas leaflet issued on Friday praised the suicide bombers but did not repeat the responsibility claim or the ultimatum.
Islamic militants opposed to Israel's existence and the PLO's interim peace deals with the Jewish state have in the past carried out suicide bombings in waves.
Wednesday's twin blasts were the first since a suicide bombing in March and the deadliest since 57 people were killed in a series of similar attacks in February and March 1996.
